title: Bounded b2b trial run
statement: Let $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ be finite-state Boolean-input Turing machines, let $x,u$ be Boolean words, let $b$ be a Boolean, and let $t_i,s_i,s_v$ be natural numbers. Suppose $M_I$ halts on input $x$ after $t_i$ steps with output $x$ and uses at most $s_i$ cells of space, and the cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on input $x\mathbin{++}u$ halts with output $b$, clears all work tapes, returns all work heads to the origin, and keeps every work head within distance $s_v$ of the origin. Starting the associated trial machine in its anchor phase with input head at position $1$, buffer $u$, and the other designated tapes blank, there is a positive time $T$ at which it is in the verdict state recording $b$, with the buffer still $u$ and the copied word $x\mathbin{++}u$ in the designated tape. At every earlier time $r$ with $0<r<T$ it is not in the anchor state, and at every $r<T$ it is not in any verdict state; through time $T$ it never halts or emits output, and every work-head position has absolute value at most $|x|+|u|+s_v+s_i+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_I$ computes output $x$ on input $x$ in time $t_i$
$M_I$ uses at most $s_i$ space on input $x$ at time $t_i$
The cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on $x\mathbin{++}u$ halts with output $b$, clears its tapes, returns heads to the origin, and uses space at most $s_v$
